note: Comparisons are restricted to the same SEC Item; one-to-many and many-to-one matches are allowed within an Item. Evidence-supported overlapping links with one shared disclosure are consolidated; original decisions are retained in grouping.source_alignments. Other supported matched groups may share disclosures while retaining their original links; overlap alone does not require review. Auto-matched means complete original text equality after bullet/whitespace normalization, with no LLM call for that link. Mixed exact/LLM groups retain each link's method in grouping.source_alignments. AI-verified means model review plus deterministic source checks, not human verification. Unmatched means a validated verifier decision found no counterpart in the comparison's saved disclosures, not proof of filing-wide absence. Current-only unmatched disclosures are introduced_disclosure; previous-only unmatched disclosures are removed_disclosure. Unmatched decisions remain needs_review until the run completes. Invalid, unfinished or conflicting decisions remain needs_review. Scope is saved narrative disclosures, not all tables or the entire filing.

alignments.explanation:
Both disclosures outline the accounting policy for amortizing finite-life intangible assets over 1-20 years using a method reflecting economic benefit consumption, or straight-line if indeterminate. 2023 cites P052_S002; 2024 cites P059_S002.

Both disclosures describe the accounting policy for acquired intangible assets. The 2023 disclosure details the valuation methods (MPEE, With/Without, Relief-from-Royalty) for specific asset types like developed technology and customer relationships. The 2024 disclosure (nvda_2024_8_D058) provides the corresponding current policy, stating that intangible assets (including developed technology and customer relationships) are amortized over periods of one to twenty years using methods reflecting the consumption pattern (which implies the same valuation/amortization principles described in 2023). They share the specific subject of 'acquired intangible asset valuation and amortization policy'.

The 2023 disclosure states that finite-lived intangible assets are amortized over estimated useful lives based on the pattern of economic benefits received, affecting cost of revenue and operating expenses. The 2024 disclosure (nvda_2024_8_D058) explicitly confirms this same policy: 'We currently amortize our intangible assets with finite lives... using a method that reflects the pattern in which the economic benefits of the intangible asset are consumed'. Both disclose the specific policy on amortization of finite-lived intangibles and the basis (pattern of economic benefits).

sentences.text: We currently amortize our intangible assets with finite lives over periods ranging from one to twenty years using a method that reflects the pattern in which the economic benefits of the intangible asset are consumed or otherwise used up or, if that pattern cannot be reliably determined, using a straight-line amortization method.
The estimated fair value and useful life of the acquired intangible assets at the time of the acquisition are as follows:
(1) The fair value of developed technology was identified using the Multi-Period Excess Earnings Method.
(2) Customer relationships represent the fair value of the existing relationships using the With and Without Method.
(3) Order backlog represents primarily the fair value of purchase arrangements with customers using the Multi-Period Excess Earnings Method.
(4) Trade names primarily relate to Mellanox trade names and fair value was determined by applying the Relief-from-Royalty Method under the income approach.
(5) The fair value of IPR&D was determined using the Multi-Period Excess Earnings Method.

The fair value of the finite-lived intangible assets will be amortized over the estimated useful lives based on the pattern in which the economic benefits are expected to be received to cost of revenue and operating expenses.

We currently amortize our intangible assets with finite lives over periods ranging from one to twenty years using a method that reflects the pattern in which the economic benefits of the intangible asset are consumed or otherwise used up or, if that pattern cannot be reliably determined, using a straight-line amortization method.

Intangible assets primarily represent acquired intangible assets including developed technology and customer relationships, as well as rights acquired under technology licenses, patents, and acquired IP.

previous_disclosures.summary: The company amortizes finite-life intangible assets over one to twenty years based on the consumption of economic benefits, using straight-line if no reliable pattern exists. Initially, in-process research and development (IPR&D) is capitalized as an indefinite-life asset, which is reclassified and amortized upon completion.

alignments.explanation:
Both disclosures describe the impairment testing methodology for long-lived assets, measuring recoverability by comparing carrying amount to undiscounted future cash flows and determining fair value via discounted cash flows. 2023 cites P053_S002, P053_S003, P053_S004; 2024 cites P060_S002, P060_S003, P060_S004.

Both disclosures address the accounting treatment for assets held for disposal, stating they are presented separately, reported at the lower of carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell, and are no longer depreciated. 2023 cites P053_S005; 2024 cites P060_S005.

sentences.text: Recoverability of assets or asset groups to be held and used is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of an asset or asset group to estimated undiscounted future cash flows expected to be generated by the asset or asset group.

If the carrying amount of an asset or asset group exceeds its estimated future cash flows, an impairment charge is recognized for the amount by which the carrying amount of the asset or asset group exceeds the estimated fair value of the asset or asset group.
Fair value is determined based on the estimated discounted future cash flows expected to be generated by the asset or asset group.

Assets and liabilities to be disposed of would be separately presented in the Consolidated Balance Sheet and the assets would be reported at the lower of the carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell, and would no longer be depreciated.

alignments.explanation:
Both disclosures describe the initial allocation of acquisition purchase price to tangible/intangible assets and liabilities, recording excess as goodwill, and note that management's fair value estimates are inherently uncertain. 2023 cites P054_S001, P054_S002, P054_S003; 2024 cites P061_S001, P061_S002, P061_S003.

Both disclosures highlight the uncertainty in valuing intangible assets, noting that estimates of future cash flows, discount rates, and asset lives may differ from actual results. 2023 cites P054_S004, P054_S005; 2024 cites P061_S004, P061_S005.

Both disclosures explain the measurement period adjustments, allowing up to one year for refinements to goodwill, with subsequent adjustments recorded to income. 2023 cites P054_S006, P054_S007; 2024 cites P061_S006, P061_S007.

The 2023 disclosure details the purchase price allocation for the Mellanox acquisition, while the 2024 disclosure (nvda_2024_8_D061) describes the general accounting policy for purchase price allocation in business combinations, including the allocation to tangible/intangible assets and goodwill. While the 2023 specific is Mellanox-specific and the 2024 is a general policy statement, they share the same specific topic of 'Purchase Price Allocation' methodology. However, since the 2024 filing does not contain a separate specific allocation table for a new major acquisition in the same detail, this alignment represents the topical match of the allocation process/policy. Note: nvda_2024_8_D061 is the best match for the general allocation logic described in D053.

sentences.text: We allocate the fair value of the purchase price of an acquisition to the tangible assets acquired, liabilities assumed, and intangible assets acquired, including IPR&D, based on their estimated fair values.
The excess of the fair value of the purchase price over the fair values of these net tangible and intangible assets acquired is recorded as goodwill.
Management's estimates of fair value are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable, but our estimates and assumptions are inherently uncertain and subject to refinement.

The estimates and assumptions used in valuing intangible assets include, but are not limited to, the amount and timing of projected future cash flows, discount rate used to determine the present value of these cash flows and asset lives.
These estimates are inherently uncertain and, therefore, actual results may differ from the estimates made.

As a result, during the measurement period of up to one year from the acquisition date, we may record adjustments to the assets acquired and liabilities assumed with the corresponding offset to goodwill.

Upon the conclusion of the measurement period or final determination of the fair value of the purchase price of an acquisition, whichever comes first, any subsequent adjustments are recorded to our Consolidated Statements of Income.

We allocated the purchase price to tangible and identified intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed based on the estimated fair values.
We allocate the fair value of the purchase price of an acquisition to the tangible assets acquired, liabilities assumed, and intangible assets acquired, based on their estimated fair values.
The excess of the fair value of the purchase price over the fair values of these net tangible and intangible assets acquired is recorded as goodwill.
Management's estimates of fair value are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable, but our estimates and assumptions are inherently uncertain and subject to refinement.

The estimates and assumptions used in valuing intangible assets include, but are not limited to, the amount and timing of projected future cash flows, discount rate used to determine the present value of these cash flows and asset lives.
These estimates are inherently uncertain and, therefore, actual results may differ from the estimates made.

As a result, during the measurement period of up to one year from the acquisition date, we may record adjustments to the assets acquired and liabilities assumed with the corresponding offset to goodwill.

Upon the measurement period's conclusion or final determination of the fair value of the purchase price of an acquisition, whichever comes first, any subsequent adjustments are recorded to our Consolidated Statements of Income.
